title: Syncing a previously deleted feed leaves its tombstone in place

evidence.quote:
feed.title = feed_data.title
                feed.is_active = feed_data.is_active
                feed.mode = feed_data.mode
                feed.max_articles = feed_data.max_articles
                feed.updated_at = datetime.utcnow()

reasoning: POST /feeds/sync looks up every existing Feed by URL, including soft-deleted rows, then updates normal fields without clearing deleted_at. The endpoint can therefore report an updated feed while the feed remains tombstoned and excluded from normal feed listing and incremental active-feed sync. The create endpoint explicitly clears deleted_at when restoring the same URL, showing the intended invariant for resurrecting a soft-deleted feed is missing here.
reproduction: Create a feed, delete it so deleted_at is set, then POST /api/feeds/sync with the same URL and is_active=true. The response reports the item as updated, but GET /api/feeds still excludes it because deleted_at remains non-null.
recommendation: When sync receives a URL whose existing row is soft-deleted, either restore it by setting deleted_at = None and updated_at = now, or reject the request with a clear conflict if tombstones must win over client pushes.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing sync test only covers creating brand-new feeds and asserts the synced count; it never syncs a URL that already exists as a tombstoned row or checks visibility after sync.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that creates a feed, deletes it, POSTs the same URL to /api/feeds/sync, then asserts the feed is no longer tombstoned and appears in GET /api/feeds, or asserts the chosen conflict response if restoration is intentionally disallowed.
minimumFixScope: Update sync_feeds handling for existing feeds with deleted_at set and add a tombstone-resync regression test.
